item.title: Smartphone-Based Irrigation Information in Vineyards
item.description: We developed a simple and fast way to estimate crop water needs in vineyards using just a smartphone and computer vision instead of expensive sensors.

item.title: Lab Receives New Grant for AI in Agriculture
item.description: Our lab has been awarded a significant new grant to advance research in artificial intelligence applications for sustainable agriculture.

item.title: Agriculture Experiential Robotics Platform
item.description: A low-cost, open-source educational robotics platform that integrates precision agriculture and automation to teach students how to sustainably grow food using real-world engineering and data-driven techniques.

item.title: Automated Vineyard Pruning Weight Estimation
item.description: We developed an inexpensive, easy-to-use smartphone-based system that estimates grapevine pruning weight using structured light and computer vision.

item.title: ViViD-5K: A Dataset and Model for Grape Cluster and Berry Segmentation
item.description: ViViD-5K is a large annotated image dataset and segmentation pipeline designed to automate grape cluster closure analysis in vineyards using computer vision.

item.title: Computer Vision-Based Yield Estimation for Precision Agriculture
item.description: A computer vision-based deep learning model for accurate and non-invasive crop yield estimation using drone and ground-based imagery, achieving 0.92 R-squared.

item.title: Deep Learning Approaches for Crop Disease Detection in Precision Agriculture
item.description: A deep learning framework achieving 95.3% accuracy in automated crop disease detection using CNNs with attention mechanisms, validated through extensive field trials.

item.description: An open-source, low-cost, soft-bodied mobile robot designed for safe, multimodal interaction in crowded and unstructured environments.

item.title: Prebloom Cluster Count Prediction in Vineyards
item.description: A low-cost, computer vision pipeline that counts grape clusters before flowering using just a smartphone and AI.

item.description: Advanced topics in computer vision techniques applied to agricultural challenges, including crop phenotyping, disease detection, and yield estimation.

item.title: Dr. Sarah Johnson
item.description:
About Me

Dr. Sarah Johnson is a Professor of Computer Science and Agricultural Engineering at Cornell University. Her research focuses on developing innovative computer vision and cyber-physical systems for precision agriculture, with the goal of making farming more efficient and sustainable.

Education

  • Ph.D. in Computer Science, Stanford University, 2010
  • M.S. in Agricultural Engineering, UC Davis, 2006
  • B.S. in Computer Engineering, MIT, 2004

Research Interests

  • Computer Vision for Plant Phenotyping
  • Autonomous Agricultural Robotics
  • Machine Learning in Precision Agriculture
  • Cyber-Physical Systems for Smart Farming

Current Projects

  • Smart Crop Monitoring: Developing AI-powered systems for real-time crop health monitoring
  • Autonomous Harvesting: Creating robotic systems for selective harvesting
  • Digital Twin Agriculture: Building virtual models of agricultural systems for optimization

Selected Publications

  1. Johnson, S., et al. (2023). “Deep Learning for Plant Disease Detection.” Nature Machine Intelligence
  2. Johnson, S., & Chen, M. (2022). “Robotic Systems in Modern Agriculture.” IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
  3. Johnson, S., et al. (2021). “Computer Vision Applications in Precision Agriculture.” Agricultural Systems

Teaching

  • CS 4320: Computer Vision
  • AGEN 5100: Precision Agriculture Systems
  • CS 6750: Machine Learning for Agriculture

Contact

Feel free to reach out if you’re interested in joining our lab or collaborating on research projects. I’m particularly interested in working with students who are passionate about applying technology to solve agricultural challenges.
